In the absence of Charlie Walker and George Flanagan, the result of this race was very much a matter for speculation. A field of 37 started, including three Essex Beagles men, and a bunch of about twelve runners was soon detached on the first lap, with Eric Gebbett in close attendance.
George Flanagan performed extremely well to win the individual title and thus follows in the footsteps of Harry Shields, Ted Stimpson and Derek Burfitt, all past winners of this race.

George Flanagan was the only one of our runners who excelled himself and he should be pleased with thirteenth position. John Moore, by finishing 52nd, gained good experience in a large field and Robin Weate, in his first year with us, showed that he is possessed of more than his fair share of pluck to finish 88th.
An outstanding performance was that of George Flanagan in being placed fifth, a performance which qualifies him for a Junior Honours Badge. Another good run was that of Robin Weate who was 21st.
George Flanagan seemed unable to get going. One had the impression that his long-striding action was out of place on this type of going; he faded to 52nd.
